lawyer:
AK Badrul Huq, Advocate ----- For the Appellant. 
Khan Saifur Rahman with Abul Kalam Azad, Advocates ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Bangladesh Water Development Board and others ----- Petitioners
Vs
Progati Prakaushali & another ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts that are necessary for the purpose of disposal of this appeal are that, the Progati Prakaushali an enlisted A class contractor of the Bangladesh Water Development Board was favored with the work of construction of RCC Jetty with approach embankment at Gorakghata Ghat in PS Moheshkhali District Cox's Bazar under Annual Development Programme, 1987-88. The estimated cost of the project was Taka 1,79,59,902.00. The detailed work order was issued by the Executive Engineer vide his memo No. 776 dated 2-5-88 and the work was scheduled to be completed by the 30th June, 1989. The respondent No. 1 contractor started the work on 12-6-88. During execution of the said project it was felt that approval of the drawing from IWTA should be taken and that would require certain time. In that view of the matter the construction of the said Jetty was suspended by the Water Development Board for the purpose of obtaining approval of the drawing from IWTA. After obtaining necessary approval from the IWTA the respondent No. 1 contractor started the construction work of the project and thereafter the project was completed by the respondent No. 1 contractor ahead of scheduled time. The work was suspended with effect from 27-6-88 to 5-8-88 for 40 days and the contractor respondent No. 1 successfully completed the work on 9-8-89 and the completion certificate was issued by the Superintending Engineer vide his Memo No. 2737 dated 4-9-1989 and the project was inaugurated by the President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh on 18th October, 1989. After completion of the project the respondent No. 1 contractor submitted his bill and claimed certain money on account of suspension of the work for 40 days. The contractor also claimed certain amount of money on account of increase in price of cement and MS rod. The respondent No. 1 contractor also claimed for bonus for early completion of the said project. During the course of execution of the project the contractor was required to do certain additional work out of tender schedule and it was agreed upon between the parties that for any additional work the contractor will be paid in the light of the rate fixed in the tender. The respondent No. 1 contractor completed all the works. These were accepted by the Engineer and thereafter submitted his claims to the appropriate authority and his claims were also recommended by the Engineer concerned yet the claims were not settled by the local authority. As such, the petitioner contractor respondent No. 1 submitted a prayer to the then Chief Engineer, South Eastern Zone of Water Development Board at Comilla to settle up the claims through arbitration. On receipt of the notice, the Chief Engineer, South Eastern Zone, Water Development Board, Comilla vide his office order dated 28-8-1991 appointed Mr. Tarikuddin Miah, Superintending Engineer, Planning and Maintenance Circle, Water Development Board Comilla as the arbitrator to arbitrate upon the dispute between the parties namely, respondent No. 1 contractor and Bangladesh Water Development Board in the matter of payment of the bills for the purpose of construction of RCC Jetty with approach embankment at Moheshkhali PS within the Cox's Bazar District. 

 3. On receipt of the office order of the Chief Engineer South Eastern Zone, Bangladesh Water Development Board, the Superintending Engineer Planning and Maintenance Circle at Comilla undertook the arbitration proceeding in the instant case and notified all the parties. It appears from the record that the Chief Engineer and Superintending Engineer of Chittagong Circle duly represented the case of Bangladesh Water Development Board before the arbitrator and the arbitrator heard the matter on several dates. On one occasion the arbitrator accompanied by the parties also visited the constructed RCC Jetty with approach embankment at Moheshkhali and thereafter he delivered his award on 27-4-1993 for a total amount of Taka 12,69,324.00 in favour of the contractor respondent No.1 but as the Chief Engineer claimed through a letter that an amount of Taka 9,85,839.00 has been over paid to the contractor respondent No.1, the learned arbitrator in the aforesaid award passed a provisional order for deducting that amount from the total amount of Taka 12,69,324.00. It also appears from the award dated 27-4-93 that the learned arbitrator also kept this issue open and gave an option to the respondent No. 1 contractor to challenge the amount claimed by the Bangladesh Water Development Board on account of over payment. It appears that after pronouncement of the preliminary award dated 27-4-1993 the contractor respondent No.1 after verifying the record challenged the contention of the Bangladesh Water Development Board that they had paid an amount of Taka 9,85,839.00 on account of over payment. The Bangladesh Water Development Board, it appears from the record, did not contest/deny this contention of the contractor respondent No. 1 and ultimately they have admitted that no amount was paid by the Water Development Board to the respondent No. 1 contractor as over payment and, as such, after hearing both the parties the learned Arbitrator vide his award dated 10-3-1994 modified his earlier award and pronounced award in favour of the respondent No. 1 contractor for an amount of Taka 12,69,324.00 on 5 counts as claimed by the respondent No. 1 contractor. 

 5. Mr. AK Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the second party appellant, submits that as per clause 26 of Tender Agreement, the Superintending Engineer of the respective circle was to be appointed as the arbitrator and the Superintending Engineer of the respective circle having not been appointed as the Arbitrator, the very appointment of the Arbitrator was illegal and without jurisdiction and the award given by illegally appointed arbitrator is also illegal and without jurisdiction and the award given by the Arbitrator is liable to be set aside and the learned Subordinate Judge did not at all consider this pertinent aspect of the matter and thus he fell into a serious error in the decision and the impugned order is liable to be set aside on this score alone. The learned Advocate further submits that the Water Development Board is the sole authority to appoint arbitrator and the Chief Engineer has got no authority whatsoever to appoint any arbitrator in the instant case and the Water Development Board having not appointed any arbitrator to settle the dispute between the parties the appointment of Superintending Engineer of another circle as the arbitrator is wholly illegal and without jurisdiction. The learned Advocate further submits that the arbitrator did not at all give any proper hearing to the appellant's side nor did he hold the proceeding properly and lawfully nor consider the legal evidence and the arbitrator misconducted the arbitration proceeding and also committed a legal misconduct and the award, thus, got no leg to stand upon and the learned Subordinate Judge did not at all consider this legal aspect of the case and by this non consideration of the legal aspect the merit of the decision of the matter has seriously been affected. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge utterly failed to consider that the arbitration proceeding was not conducted in accordance with law and that the arbitrator in giving the award acted beyond the power vested in him and thus fell into an error in not setting aside the award. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in holding that the objection filed by the opposite party of the Miscellaneous case has not been filed within the stipulated period and the said finding is absolutely misconceived and not tenable in law. The learned Advocate finally submits that the award having been wholly illegal, void and without jurisdiction, the same was liable to be set aside no matter whether the appellant Water Development Board has filed any written objection under section 33 of the Arbitration Act or not and. the learned Subordinate Judge committed a gross illegality in making an illegal award rule of the court. 

 7. Mr. Khan Saifur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the contractor respondent No. 1, on the other hand, submits that the instant appeal is incompetent inasmuch it is provided in section 17 of the Arbitration Act that judgment of the court shall be followed by a decree but in the instant case no decree has yet been drawn and in that view of the matter the present appeal is incompetent on the ground of prematurity. Mr. Khan further submits that the written objection filed by the second party appellant cannot be treated as an application under section 33 of the Arbitration Act inasmuch as an application under section 33 of the said Act is an independent proceeding and that cannot be initiated by a party who wants to raise objection as to the legality and validity on the ground as laid down in section 30 of the Arbitration Act. He thus submits that an application under section 33 of the Arbitration Act can be used by a party as a sword against another but not as a shield in defence as the second party appellant did in the instant case inasmuch as they have filed the same in the garb of an objection in the arbitration proceeding. He further submits that when a party files an application under section 33 of the Arbitration Act the onus is on him to bring home the allegation levelled in that application and when a party files a written objection against an award under section 17 of the Arbitration Act the onus is shifted to the other party and in that view of the matter this written objection filed by the second party appellant before the learned Subordinate Judge cannot be treated as an application under section 33 of the Arbitration Act. The learned Advocate further submits that even if it is assumed to be an application under section 33 of the Arbitration Act then also the findings of the learned Subordinate Judge that the application is barred by limitation and that the abjection is not tenable in law for noncompliance of proviso to section 33 of the Arbitration Act is absolutely correct and in that view of the matter he submits that the learned Subordinate Judge in the instant case rightly kept this written objection out of his consideration by rightly holding that the same is barred by limitation and is not tenable in law due to non deposit of money as is required under section 33 of the Arbitration Act. Mr. Khan finally submits that the submission that the learned Arbitrator had no jurisdiction to take the arbitration proceeding in the instant case is absolutely erroneous and without any materials basis. By referring to the memo dated 28-7-91 issued by the then Chief Engineer South Eastern Zone, Bangladesh Power Development Board, Comilla Circle, he submits that from this memo it is crystal clear that at the relevant time the Chief Engineer of South Eastern Zone of Bangladesh Water Development Board was the competent authority under whom the concerned Superintending Engineer and Executive Engineer were placed and in pursuance of office order dated 6-6-91 the Chief Engineer appointed the Superintending Engineer, Planning and Maintenance, Comilla circle as arbitrator to arbitrate upon the dispute between the parties and a copy of the office order was endorsed to the Superintending Engineer, Planning and Operation Chittagong Circle and the Executive Engineer, Planning and Maintenance, Cox's Bazar Division for necessary action. From this office order and subsequent conduct of the second party appellant it is crystal clear that they willingly and voluntarily surrendered to the jurisdiction of the arbitrator in the instant case and at no stage till the pronouncement of the award by the arbitrator did they come up with any allegation on the ground of jurisdiction and as such the plea of the second party appellant that the arbitrator in the instant case had no jurisdiction whatsoever to arbitrate up the dispute is not tenable in law and they must be estopped from raising such plea after signing and delivery of the concerned award and for that purpose he refers to and relies on the decision reported in 9 PLD 1960 (Lahore) 677. 

 13. Mr. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate for the second party appellant in course of his submission relied on the resolution dated 27-7-1985 passed by the Bangladesh Water Development Board amending clause 26 of Form T-1 wherein a new provision has been inserted by amending the original clause 26 of the said Form and under the amended provision a time limit of 3 months has been inserted and also provided that when a dispute arises between the parties the aggrieved party must refer the dispute within 3 months to the Chairman of the Bangladesh Water Development Board and on receipt of the notice of the aggrieved party the Chairman of the Water Development Board will appoint an Arbitrator to adjudicate upon the dispute between the parties. Neither party disputes as to the genuinity of this document which is annexed at page 119 of the paper book but we are of the opinion that this document is absolutely irrelevant for the purpose of disposal of the instant revisional application inasmuch as though this a resolution dated 20-7-1985 but the Bangladesh Water Development Board deliberately did not incorporate this clause in their contract which was entered into between the contractor and the Bangladesh Water Development Board for the purpose of construction of RCC Jetty with approach embankment at Gorakghata Ghat in Police Station Moheshkhali, District Cox's Bazar. The Water Development Board in the instant case inserted the original clause 26 of Form T-l which provides that if any dispute arises between the parties arising out of the Contract the dispute shall be referred to the Superintending Engineer of the Circle for the time being holding the office at the time of hearing of the arbitration for the time being in force who after such investigation as he may think proper shall deliver his award which shall be final, conclusive and binding on all the parties to this contract and relying on this clause he submits that the notices of arbitration served by the contractor respondent No.1 coupled with the relevant office order issued by the Executive Engineer, South Eastern Zone, Water Development Board dated 25-7-91 conclusively establish beyond any shadow of doubt that the Superintending Engineer at the relevant time was the Superintending Engineer of the Chittagong Circle and the appointment of the Superintending Engineer of Planning and Maintenance Division Comilla Circle by the then Chief Engineer of South Eastern Zone of Bangladesh Water Development Board is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction and the whole arbitration proceedings is absolutely without jurisdiction and, as such, void ab initio and for this purpose Mr. Huq relied on the decision reported in 6 DLR 477, wherein it has been held that where an award is illegal and void ab initio and the illegality is apparent on the face of it, the court should take judicial notice of it, and it is not necessary that the parties should file objections to the award under section 30 within the time prescribed under Article 158 of the Limitation Act. 

 20. In the case reported in PLD 1960 (Lahore) 677, the General Manager of the North Western Railway appointed the then Chief Engineer as the arbitrator and in the arbitration clause there was a stipulation that in the any dispute arising between the parties the General Manager shall appoint arbitrator and in pursuance of that arbitration clause the General Manager of the Railway appointed the Chief Engineer as arbitrator but during continuance of the arbitration proceedings the Chief Engineer was promoted to the rank of General Manager and he continued with the arbitration proceeding and none of the parties raised any objection as to the continuation of the arbitration proceeding by him. After pronouncement of the award, the party against whom the award went raised an objection that the arbitrator had no jurisdiction to arbitrate upon the dispute after his promotion to the post of General Manager but that contention of the party was repelled by the Lahore High Court observing that the respondent was fully aware of the whole circumstances and raised no objection either to the original appointment or to his continuance as arbitrator after becoming General Manager and, as such, he is estopped by his conduct from challenging the jurisdiction to act as such and further held that the position later occupied by the arbitration did not disqualify him to act as arbitrator. 

 21. Yet there is another aspect of this case. It is found from the application filed by the contractor respondent No. 1 under section 14(2) of the "Arbitration Act that at the relevant time the office of the Chief Engineer, South Eastern Zone, Bangladesh Water Development Board, the proforma defendant opposite party No. 13 was the controlling authority of the construction work. His office was situated at Comilla and in the mean time because of reorganisation of the office of proforma opposite party No. 2 i.e. the office of the Chief Engineer, South Eastern Zone, Bangladesh Water Development Board, has been shifted to Chittagong at the address given in the cause title of the appeal. From the statements of facts made by the contractor respondent No. 1 in paragraph 2 of the application under section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act it appears that at the relevant time the Chief Engineer, South Eastern Zone, was the controlling authority of the project and his office was situated at Comilla and, as such, it appears beyond doubt that at the relevant time the Superintending Engineer, Planning and Maintenance, Comilla Circle was the competent Engineer to take up the arbitration proceeding. The assertion made by the respondent No. 1 in paragraph No. 2 of his application under section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act has neither been denied nor controverted by the Second Party appellant before the Subordinate Judge nor they have called in question these assertions made by the contractor respondent No.1 in that application even before this court. In view of uncontroverted factual position of the case it appears to us that the Superintending Engineer. Planning and Maintenance, Comilla Circle, was the competent Engineer to arbitrate the dispute. Further, the decisions referred to and relied on by Mr. Haque namely 6 DLR, 8 DLR and P LD 1966, Dhaka, show that in these decisions the then Dhaka High Court held that if on the face of record it is found that the award suffers from gross illegality the same becomes a nullity in the eye of law and then the court can take judicial notice of it. Moreover, the facts of those cases differ from the facts of the present case. In those cases it was found by the High Court that the arbitrators were not legally appointed and as such the award declared by them was a nullity in the eye of law. In our opinion the facts of the cases reported in PLD (Kar) 245, AIR 1941 (Mad) 129, AIR 1945 (Born) 497 and PLD 1960 (Lah) 677 are similar to the facts of the present case and principles of law enunciated in those decisions are applicable to the present case. Moreover, as a matter of fact also we have found that the Superintending Engineer, Planning and Maintenance, Comilla Circle was correctly appointed arbitrator in the instant case and none of the parties raised their objections as to the competence of the arbitrator to deal with the matter in dispute and even if there had been any irregularity in the appointment of the arbitrator that irregularity has been cured by the conduct of the parties. On a scrutiny of the materials and evidence on record we are of the opinion that by no stretch of imagination it can be said that the award dated 27-4-1993 and 10-3-1994 appear to be a nullity on the face of it. In a scrutiny of the materials and evidence on record we do not find any ground to hold that the arbitrator had ever misconducted himself or misconducted the proceeding nor the other elements of section 30 of the Arbitration Act are present in the instant case and in that view of the matter it is very difficult on our part to dislodge the positive finding given by the learned Subordinate Judge that there is nothing on record to interfere with the award given by the arbitrator. In this view of the matter we do not find any substance in the submission made of Mr. Huq on the point of jurisdiction of the arbitrator on merits.
